items.question: Which TWO capabilities does tool use (function calling) add to a Claude integration that are not available in plain chat? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The ability to retrieve live, up-to-date data from external systems during a response
options.B: A higher output token limit that allows longer generated responses
options.C: The ability to take actions such as writing to a database or submitting a form
options.D: A dedicated context cache that avoids re-sending the same document on repeat calls
options.E: Guaranteed prevention of responses that draw on the model's parametric memory

items.question: Prompt caching delivers the greatest reduction in cost and latency when which condition is present?

options.A: The model is generating very long outputs for a single complex task
options.B: Each API call introduces entirely new content and no prior context is reused
options.C: A large block of context — such as a system prompt or reference document — is sent unchanged across many separate API calls
options.D: Fine-tuning has been applied so the model already has relevant context embedded in its weights

items.question: Rate limits on the Claude API are BEST characterised as a constraint on which architectural dimension?

options.A: Throughput — the number of requests or tokens processed per unit of time — requiring teams to design for queuing and pacing
options.B: Accuracy — the proportion of responses meeting quality thresholds before a retry is permitted
options.C: Availability — the number of hours per day the API can be called before a daily outage window begins
options.D: Security — the maximum number of unique callers allowed on a single API key before rotation is required

items.question: A team specifies an explicit model version in their API configuration rather than using a generic 'latest' alias. What is the PRIMARY motivation?

options.A: Explicit versions are priced lower because they run on older infrastructure
options.B: Using 'latest' creates a single point of failure if the provider retires the alias
options.C: Regulatory frameworks require all AI outputs be reproducible, which the 'latest' alias makes impossible
options.D: A new model release may subtly change output style or reasoning in ways that break downstream processing or validation logic

items.question: Which TWO statements correctly describe what the Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides to a technical integration? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A standardised interface that allows Claude to connect to external tools and data sources without bespoke custom code for each integration
options.B: An encryption layer that prevents prompt injection from any external data source connected through MCP
options.C: A protocol for describing what tools and resources a server exposes, so a Claude-powered application can discover and call them consistently
options.D: A model-specific routing mechanism that automatically selects the best model tier for each tool call
options.E: A replacement for API keys that authenticates Claude directly with external systems using enterprise SSO

items.question: Which scenario represents a case where fine-tuning would be justified over prompt engineering alone?

options.A: The team wants Claude to follow a specific output format that a well-structured prompt could specify
options.B: Claude is producing generic answers because the system prompt does not include enough background context
options.C: The organisation needs Claude to match a highly specific house style whose nuances cannot be reliably captured in a prompt
options.D: Claude occasionally adds unnecessary caveats that a negative constraint in the prompt would remove

items.question: What distinguishes a formal evaluation (eval) programme from ad-hoc spot-checking of Claude's outputs?

options.A: Evals produce systematic, repeatable, statistically comparable measurements over a defined test set; spot-checking yields anecdotal impressions from a subset of live outputs
options.B: Evals are run only at initial deployment; spot-checking provides ongoing quality measurement once the system is in production
options.C: Evals require direct API access; spot-checking is the quality discipline for chat-interface users
options.D: Evals are certified by the model provider; spot-checking is the organisation's own independent review

items.question: Which TWO characteristics correctly describe Claude Code, distinguishing it from the Claude.ai chat interface? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Claude Code is restricted to interactive sessions and cannot run in automated pipelines or CI workflows
options.B: Claude Code operates within a developer's local environment and can read, write, and execute files directly
options.C: Claude Code generates code that runs on Anthropic's servers rather than the user's local machine
options.D: Claude Code can be invoked non-interactively in automation scripts and CI/CD pipelines
options.E: Claude Code requires a separately fine-tuned model not available through the standard Claude API

items.question: A developer sets temperature to its lowest value for a document classification pipeline. What is the PRIMARY effect?

options.A: The model generates shorter outputs to reduce processing time
options.B: The model's outputs become more deterministic, with less variation across equivalent inputs
options.C: The model applies more conservative safety filters to sensitive classifications
options.D: The model's context window expands to allow longer documents to be processed

items.question: Which TWO conditions MOST favour choosing long context over retrieval-augmented generation? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The document corpus is small enough to fit within the context window at acceptable per-call cost
options.B: The corpus spans thousands of documents that collectively exceed any practical context window capacity
options.C: Query volume is high enough that the token cost of including the full corpus on every call would be prohibitive
options.D: The corpus changes rarely and nearly every query draws on content spread across the full document set
options.E: Questions are narrow enough that only two or three specific passages need to be surfaced per query

items.question: In the context of the Claude API, what is a token?

options.A: A secure credential used to authenticate API calls
options.B: The basic unit of text the model processes and charges for, roughly three-quarters of an English word on average
options.C: A timestamped record of each API call used for billing reconciliation
options.D: A permission grant that controls which model tiers a user can access

items.question: When does an agentic workflow provide a clear advantage over a single-shot prompt?

options.A: When the desired output is a short summary rather than a long document
options.B: When the task requires multiple model tiers to be consulted in sequence
options.C: When the task requires taking actions or retrieving dynamic information before producing a final result
options.D: When the team wants to prevent the context window from filling during a long conversation

items.question: Which type of professional is the primary intended beneficiary of Claude Code?

options.A: Software developers working in a codebase who need an AI agent to navigate, edit, and run code locally
options.B: Business analysts who want AI-generated code snippets to paste into spreadsheet formulas
options.C: IT administrators managing user access and permissions for Claude deployments
options.D: Data scientists who need to run model training jobs on Anthropic's cloud infrastructure

items.question: In an API-based product, which element is MOST appropriate for instructions that must apply identically to every user session?

options.A: A per-user message prepended at the start of each conversation
options.B: A Project knowledge document that users can read and update themselves
options.C: The final message in each conversation, summarising the desired behaviour
options.D: The system prompt, set by the application developer and not visible to end users

items.question: Which technique reduces per-call token cost when a large, unchanging context is reused across thousands of API requests?

options.A: Batch processing, by grouping the requests into a single asynchronous job
options.B: Prompt caching, by storing the repeated prefix so it is not reprocessed on each call
options.C: Fine-tuning, by encoding the context into the model's weights so it need not be sent at all
options.D: Temperature reduction, by constraining output to the most probable tokens

items.question: A document corpus has grown to several thousand pages and is queried dozens of times per minute. Which architecture is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Retrieval-augmented generation, fetching only relevant passages for each query
options.B: Long context, loading all documentation into the context window on each call
options.C: Fine-tuning, embedding the documentation into the model's weights
options.D: Batch processing, submitting all queries as overnight jobs when cost is lower

items.question: What does a formal evaluation (eval) programme PRIMARILY measure?

options.A: The throughput of the API pipeline in requests per minute
options.B: The financial cost of running Claude across all organisational use cases
options.C: The quality of Claude's outputs against a defined test set and scoring criteria
options.D: The security posture of the API integration against external threats

items.question: A business professional is writing a requirements document for a developer implementing a Claude integration. Which element is MOST important to include?

options.A: The specific SDK method names the developer should call to invoke the API
options.B: The exact temperature value and token budget the developer must not exceed
options.C: A list of third-party libraries compatible with the Anthropic SDK
options.D: A description of the desired input/output behaviour, the target user, and the constraints on what Claude should and should not do

items.question: Which TWO factors would favour hosting Claude through a cloud provider rather than calling the Anthropic API directly? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Cloud providers offer lower per-token pricing than the direct Anthropic API
options.B: The organisation's data-residency policy requires AI processing within a specific geographic region supported by that cloud provider
options.C: Cloud providers automatically improve model quality by fine-tuning on the organisation's traffic
options.D: The team wants to consolidate AI spend on an existing cloud commitment or enterprise agreement
options.E: Cloud-hosted Claude models have a larger context window than those available through the direct API

items.question: Which symptom MOST clearly indicates that a conversation thread is approaching context window capacity?

options.A: The model begins to omit details from early in the conversation that it correctly referenced in earlier turns
options.B: The model starts generating shorter responses to conserve available tokens
options.C: The API returns a rate-limit error on the next call in the sequence
options.D: The model's output becomes grammatically fragmented, with incomplete sentences

items.question: Which TWO properties distinguish a structured eval programme from informal spot-checking? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Eval results are reproducible and can be directly compared across prompt versions or model changes
options.B: Evals are run exclusively by the model provider as part of a quality certification process
options.C: Evals use a defined test set and scoring criteria that produce aggregate quality metrics
options.D: Spot-checking requires the same test infrastructure as a formal eval but is run on a shorter schedule
options.E: Evals are only meaningful when applied to outputs from a fine-tuned model

items.question: What does enterprise SSO integration for Claude PRIMARILY govern, compared with API key management?

options.A: SSO controls which model tier employees can use; API keys control which documents they can access
options.B: SSO controls which employees can access Claude and enforces the organisation's identity policies; API key management governs programmatic credentials for applications
options.C: SSO is required for API access; API keys are required for chat-interface access
options.D: SSO limits the token consumption per employee per session; API keys control batch processing quotas

items.question: A team is building a brainstorming tool designed to generate varied, non-repetitive ideas in response to the same prompt. Which temperature setting is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Temperature at or near zero, to ensure deterministic and repeatable outputs
options.B: A moderate temperature applied only to the system prompt instructions, not the user turn
options.C: A higher temperature setting, to increase the variety of tokens sampled during generation
options.D: Temperature should match the number of ideas requested — one unit per idea

items.question: What is the key structural difference between a Claude integration using direct tool use and one built on MCP?

options.A: Direct tool use requires fine-tuning; MCP works with any standard Claude model
options.B: MCP enables higher token throughput than tool calls implemented directly in the integration code
options.C: Direct tool use is synchronous; MCP is an asynchronous batch mechanism for tool calls
options.D: MCP provides a standardised protocol for discovering and invoking tools across systems; direct tool use requires bespoke implementation code for each tool or integration

items.question: In a long agentic session, the model begins to contradict instructions that were correct in its first few responses. No new instructions have been added. What is the MOST likely technical cause?

options.A: The original instructions have scrolled outside the active context window and are no longer influencing the response
options.B: Temperature drifted upward over the course of the session, increasing output randomness
options.C: The system prompt was overwritten by a user turn containing conflicting instructions
options.D: Rate limits caused earlier tokens to be dropped from the response before they could be processed

items.question: What is the key distinction between an agent and a developer-scripted multi-step pipeline?

options.A: An agent uses multiple model tiers in sequence; a pipeline uses only one tier throughout
options.B: An agent decides which actions to take at each step based on intermediate results; a pipeline executes a fixed sequence of steps determined in advance by the developer
options.C: A pipeline cannot call external tools; an agent is the only pattern that supports tool use
options.D: An agent produces a single consolidated response; a pipeline produces an intermediate result at each step

items.question: A developer connects Claude to a web scraping tool. A page Claude retrieves contains hidden text instructing Claude to disregard its system prompt. What risk does this illustrate?

options.A: API key rotation failure — the key used to access the external site has been compromised
options.B: Context window overflow — the retrieved content is too large for the available token budget
options.C: Prompt injection — adversarial instructions embedded in external content attempt to hijack Claude's behaviour
options.D: Rate limit exhaustion — the volume of retrieved content triggers a throughput cap

items.question: Which TWO properties are characteristic of retrieval-augmented generation but NOT of the long-context approach? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Only a subset of the available documents is processed by the model on each query
options.B: The model can synthesise information across every document in the corpus simultaneously
options.C: A separate retrieval step selects which passages to include before the model generates a response
options.D: The model can reference documents that are too large to fit in the context window
options.E: Output accuracy depends entirely on what was present in the training data

items.question: When estimating the operating cost of a Claude-powered pipeline at scale, which input is MOST critical to quantify accurately?

options.A: The number of developers who will maintain the integration code
options.B: The number of unique users accessing the application each month
options.C: The geographic region where the API is hosted
options.D: The average token volume per call multiplied by the number of API calls per day

items.question: An enterprise is deploying Claude to thousands of employees. Which TWO controls belong primarily on the centralised IT/admin side rather than in individual employees' behaviours? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Configuring SSO so that Claude access is provisioned through the organisation's identity provider
options.B: Training employees on how to write effective prompts for their job function
options.C: Establishing role-based access controls that restrict which Projects or capabilities different employee groups can use
options.D: Encouraging employees to review Claude's outputs before sending them externally
options.E: Creating team-level prompt templates that reflect departmental workflows

items.question: What is the PRIMARY risk of using a 'latest' alias for model selection in a production API pipeline?

options.A: The alias always points to the most expensive tier, increasing cost without notice
options.B: A new model release may be silently assigned to the alias, changing the pipeline's output behaviour without the team's knowledge
options.C: The 'latest' alias is deprecated more frequently than versioned identifiers, creating outage risk
options.D: The alias is rate-limited more aggressively than explicit versioned model calls

items.question: What is the MOST direct symptom when an API pipeline exceeds its rate limit?

options.A: API calls begin to fail or return throttling errors rather than model responses
options.B: The model's output quality degrades as fewer tokens are allocated per response
options.C: The context window shrinks to accommodate fewer tokens per unit of time
options.D: The pipeline switches automatically to a lower-tier model to maintain throughput

items.question: What does setting temperature to its lowest value guarantee in a document classification pipeline?

options.A: Shorter output responses to reduce token consumption per call
options.B: Outputs that comply more strictly with safety policies for sensitive content
options.C: Consistent, near-deterministic label assignments for the same input across multiple runs
options.D: Faster response times due to reduced token sampling computation

items.question: A long-running conversation gradually produces outputs that drift away from the original project constraints. No instructions have been changed. What is the MOST likely cause?

options.A: The system prompt was automatically compressed to make room for new conversation turns
options.B: Temperature gradually increased over the course of the session, raising output randomness
options.C: The user's recent inputs are reinforcing a different direction through accumulated conversational emphasis
options.D: The context window is filling with conversation history, pushing the original constraints toward or beyond the effective window boundary

items.question: A RAG system consistently misses relevant content when answering queries on a specific topic. The content exists in the corpus. What is the MOST likely cause?

options.A: The retrieval step fails to surface those passages because their embedding or index representation does not align with how the queries are phrased
options.B: The model's context window is too small to include the retrieved passages alongside the full query
options.C: The topic is outside the model's training data so it cannot interpret retrieved passages even when found
options.D: Batch processing is being used for the retrieval step, causing results to arrive after the model has already generated a response

items.question: A batch job returns a high proportion of outputs that appear to misclassify the input records. What should the team check FIRST?

options.A: Whether the model version changed automatically between submission and completion
options.B: Whether the prompt and input format used in the batch call match what was validated in synchronous testing
options.C: Whether the rate limit was exceeded during the batch job, causing incomplete results
options.D: Whether the batch job was routed to a different geographic region, altering model output

items.question: During a multi-step agentic task, one tool call returns an error. What is the MOST likely effect if the failure is not explicitly handled?

options.A: The agent automatically retries the tool call up to a predefined number of attempts before halting
options.B: The agent completes remaining steps using parametric memory without noting any gap in the response
options.C: The agent may proceed with incomplete or incorrect information, compounding the error in subsequent reasoning steps
options.D: The agent halts the entire task and returns an explicit error notification to the operator

items.question: A team enables prompt caching but observes no measurable reduction in per-call cost. What is the MOST likely reason?

options.A: The model tier they are using does not support prompt caching
options.B: The system prompt is shorter than the minimum length required to register a cache checkpoint
options.C: Prompt caching only applies to output tokens, not to input token processing
options.D: The content of the prompt changes substantially on every call, preventing a stable cached prefix from forming

items.question: A team has used the same eval test set for 18 months without updating it. The production system now handles a wider range of inputs than the test set covers. What risk does this create?

options.A: Eval scores will appear stable or improving even as real-world quality degrades on input types the test set does not represent
options.B: The eval programme will begin generating false positives that inflate the perceived failure rate
options.C: The model provider will invalidate evaluation scores from test sets not refreshed within a defined period
options.D: Eval scores will fluctuate unpredictably because stale test items introduce random noise into the scoring algorithm

items.question: After fine-tuning on domain-specific examples, a model performs worse on general-purpose tasks it previously handled well. What phenomenon does this illustrate?

options.A: Prompt drift, where fine-tuning changes the model's calibration for how it interprets instructions
options.B: Catastrophic forgetting, where training on new examples degrades performance on capabilities not represented in the fine-tuning data
options.C: Rate limit collateral damage, where fine-tuning requests consume quota that otherwise serves production calls
options.D: Context window compression, where fine-tuning reduces effective context capacity for out-of-domain inputs

items.question: Which TWO scenarios describe situations where an agentic workflow would be LESS appropriate than a simpler approach? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The task is well-defined, all necessary information is already in the context, and a single model pass will produce a correct result
options.B: The task requires checking a live API for current pricing before generating a recommendation
options.C: Every step of the process is fully predictable and the developer can express the entire sequence as a fixed, scripted pipeline
options.D: The task involves synthesising information from multiple documents that have all been uploaded to the context
options.E: The model must decide which of several tools to invoke based on the content of an incoming user request

items.question: A classification pipeline begins returning inconsistent labels for identical inputs across different runs. The prompt and model have not changed. What is the MOST likely cause?

options.A: The context window is filling with cached results from prior runs, introducing label variation
options.B: The model version was silently updated when the 'latest' alias was used
options.C: Temperature is set high enough to introduce meaningful randomness into token selection, causing different labels to emerge across runs
options.D: The batch processing queue is returning results out of order, mismatching inputs to labels

items.question: A team tracks only one metric in their eval programme — the percentage of outputs that pass a length check. What key risk does this single-metric approach create?

options.A: The length metric will gradually inflate, causing the eval to report false improvements over time
options.B: The model provider may flag the metric as non-standard and decline to support it
options.C: The eval framework will malfunction if the metric does not include a semantic quality rubric
options.D: Systematic quality failures that do not manifest as length violations — such as factual errors or wrong tone — will be invisible to the eval programme

items.question: A developer has written a system prompt restricting Claude to a single product domain. A user pastes a long document ending with text instructing Claude to ignore the system prompt. What vulnerability does this attempt exploit?

options.A: The boundary between operator instructions and user-supplied data — if Claude treats the embedded instructions as authoritative, the system prompt constraints are circumvented
options.B: A context window overflow that pushes the system prompt outside the active context when long documents are added
options.C: Temperature drift triggered by long input processing, which increases the likelihood of Claude deviating from its instructions
options.D: API key compromise, as the user has gained operator-level access by injecting content into the user turn

items.question: A team discovers that an API key was included in a help document shared with 200 employees. What is the CORRECT FIRST action?

options.A: Change all employee passwords to prevent the key from being used alongside their credentials
options.B: Immediately revoke the API key in the provider console and issue a replacement, then audit recent API usage for anomalies
options.C: Remove the key from the document and remind employees it is confidential, then monitor for unauthorised use
options.D: Contact the model provider to freeze the account while the scope of potential misuse is assessed

items.question: Which TWO conditions can cause a RAG system to return a confident-sounding but factually incorrect response? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The model's context window is larger than the number of passages the retrieval step returns per query
options.B: The retrieved passages contain information that was accurate when indexed but has since become outdated
options.C: The query volume exceeds the synchronous rate limit, causing some retrieval steps to time out
options.D: The retrieval step returns passages that are topically adjacent but do not contain the correct answer, and the model infers a plausible response from the incomplete evidence

items.question: A team's actual API costs in production ran four times higher than their pre-launch estimate. Which factor MOST commonly explains this gap?

options.A: The model provider increased per-token pricing between the testing and production phases
options.B: The platform automatically upgraded the model tier for production traffic without notification
options.C: Test cost estimates were based on message length alone, while production input tokens include the full system prompt and accumulated conversation history on every call
options.D: The production deployment was routed through a cloud provider that added a substantial hosting markup

items.question: Which TWO situations demonstrate that SSO integration alone is insufficient to fully govern Claude access in an enterprise? (Choose TWO)

options.A: An employee accesses Claude via a personal account on their work device, bypassing the corporate SSO-protected instance
options.B: The SSO provider experiences an outage that temporarily prevents all employees from logging in
options.C: An employee pastes confidential client data into a Claude prompt in violation of the data-handling policy
options.D: A third-party application uses an API key rather than SSO to connect to Claude, operating entirely outside the SSO governance perimeter
options.E: A manager asks their team to use Claude for a use case not covered by the organisation's approved task list

items.question: A team upgrades from a mid-tier to the highest-tier model to fix poor output quality. After the switch, quality is unchanged. What is the MOST likely explanation?

options.A: The highest-tier model uses a different authentication method that was not correctly configured
options.B: The platform automatically reduces temperature for highest-tier calls, which lowered output variety
options.C: The highest-tier model has a smaller context window than the mid-tier model, exacerbating context pressure
options.D: The problem lies in underspecified or incomplete prompt instructions; additional reasoning depth cannot compensate for missing or unclear input information

items.question: Which TWO failure modes are MOST specific to agentic systems and do not typically apply to single-shot prompting? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The model generates a response that does not match the requested output format
options.B: An error in an early tool call introduces incorrect data that subsequent reasoning steps compound into a more serious final error
options.C: The model's output is shorter than the user expected given the task complexity
options.D: The model takes an irreversible real-world action — such as sending a message or updating a record — based on a flawed intermediate reasoning step
